title: V1 evidence blocker closure, V1-S5-013-PR1
description: How V1-S5-013-PR1 closed the five release blockers V1-S5-006-PR2 raised: the records its reruns added and every other register change, each with its value before and after; how each new executed record identifies the repository code that ran; one disposition per blocker, using one of three closure mechanisms; and the release gate that is current. The completeness ledger's own blockers and gate are left as that change decided them.

closureMechanisms.meaning: A new execution against a named repository revision, with its own record under the claim; the older record is kept and not edited.
Committed evidence that already existed, executed the claim-material components, and identifies its code, cited for the exact statement.
The statement narrowed or the status moved, through this ledger, so that the claim says only what identified evidence supports.

findings.observation: The 2026-09-03 baseline records give the descriptor's SHA-256 as ea98ce3f6cb5d0d94c1de6ad55e211ccaf3c75b01bfa3099e218a100eecdddea. That is the descriptor committed in d604077 with CRLF line endings, a Windows checkout's bytes; its committed content hashes to 03ea54d5eb321dacd95637484c6727e95f3c2c2cd52c00e58fe088e9d72a9c7c, and the file is unchanged since.
findings.resolution: Recorded, not corrected: the old record is dated history. The rerun's record gives the committed-content hash and says the two hashes are one content, so the rerun used the method the 2026-09-03 run registered.

findings.observation: The completeness check recorded that the experiment API image names no source. The three Kubernetes reruns deployed an API image built from the clone at the named revision minutes before, localhost/inferops-api@sha256:6d565a391412c74a9c0eb1bf31da216b7edb739a906bbd1827ee8a45b74d9b40, whose build the preparation transcript records.
findings.resolution: For these three records the image's source is the named revision. The limitation stands for the earlier runs, which are unchanged.

findings.observation: The scratch script that read the cluster's survival facts sources the repository's lib.sh, which stops a script at a failed command, so when the release namespace was absent it printed nothing after that lookup. It happened on the first reading and the last.
findings.resolution: The scoped-cleanup record says which lines are absent and why. No statement rests on them: nothing can be inside a namespace that does not exist, and Terraform's output records the claim's destruction.
